item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00467","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C10","C03","C20"],"selected_candidate_label":"C10","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C10 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both orders regulate allowances for members of the uniformed services under the Career Compensation Act of 1949; most decisively, the child's definition of “entitled to receive basic pay” reproduces C10's definition nearly verbatim. Both also use the same machinery authorizing service officials to issue supplementary, nonconflicting regulations that are to be uniform across the services as far as practicable. C03 and C20 contain closely parallel supplementary-regulation clauses, but neither matches the child's substantive basic-pay definition as C10 does.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The term \"entitled to receive basic pay\" shall apply to a member while on the active list or while required to perform duty in accordance with law for which he is entitled to basic pay; Provided, that such term shall not apply to any member while absent from duty under conditions which, under laws governing the particular service concerned, would prevent him from receiving full basic pay.","parent_excerpt":"The term \"entitled to receive basic pay\" shall be considered applicable to members while they are on the active list or while they are required to perform duty in accordance with law for which they are entitled to basic pay: Provided, that such term shall not be applicable to any member while absent from duty under conditions which, under laws governing the particular service concerned, would prevent him from receiving full basic pay.","explanation":"This is a nearly verbatim substantive definition, with only minor grammatical substitutions."},{"child_excerpt":"The Secretaries concerned ... are hereby authorized to prescribe such supplementary regulations not inconsistent herewith as they may deem necessary or desirable for carrying out these regulations, and such supplementary regulations shall be uniform for all the services to the fullest extent practicable.","parent_excerpt":"The Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, and the Federal Security Administrator ... are hereby authorized ... to prescribe such supplemental regulations, not inconsistent herewith, as they may deem necessary or desirable for carrying out the provisions of this order ... Provided, that such regulations shall be uniform so far as practicable for all the services concerned.","explanation":"Both employ materially the same decentralized rulemaking mechanism and uniformity requirement for the uniformed services."}]}
